entries.group: ORDER: a list the record carries whose order no consumer reads
entries.grounds: `required` (adapters.py:172) goes to three places only: review_ocr.coverage(), whose first statement is `required = sorted(set(required))` (review_ocr.py:80), so its `missing[:10]` and reasons do not depend on the caller's order; review_ocr.findings() `set(required)` (membership only); and the session record (adapters.py:220 -> run.py:491 -> RUN.json). The mutant yields git's own row order, which equals sorted() for every ASCII or valid-UTF-8 path (tree order = byte order of the full names = code-point order). It differs only where git's bytes and the decoded text disagree (an invalid UTF-8 byte under the allowlisted core.quotepath=false decodes to U+FFFD): then one list in RUN.json is ordered differently. Hence AUDITED, not EQUIVALENT. Nothing reads that order.

entries.group: T01-LABEL-PLANID: an id label inside an identity that is already distinct by hash
entries.grounds: Differential run (diff_probe.py): the only paths of `out` that differ are /plan/id ('PLAN-calc2-continued' -> 'PLAN-calc2') and /plan/plan_hash (which binds the id); the report is identical. End to end (gen_probe.py) with the mutant: child bundle loads; `execute(predecessor=...)` commits CARRIED; plan/frozen plan_id == the parent's id and plan_hash == the bundle's; verify() VERIFIED []; a second continue_from works. Everything derives from the stored bundle, so the value is consistent where it flows (plan/frozen story_runner.py:138, plan/static-admitted static_admission.py:298, 'no obligation in plan' texts story_runner.py:153, story_admission.py:147, PlanNotAdmitted :308). The only 'once' rules on plan_id are per journal (journal/format3.py:168-169; qualification_counters.py:36) and the child writes its own journal (run.py docstring :329-330, out.mkdir :345). Nothing compares ids across runs: lineage.py and verify.py name no plan id; run.py:338-375 reads the parent's record presence, anchor, claim and accounts and records plan_hash. `bundle migrate` (bundle_cli.py:127) already re-issues a plan with the SAME id and another hash, so the id is a label and the hash the identity. The child's plan_hash differs from the parent's irrespective of the suffix: every done story's obligations get story_id = `carried`, a name :416-417 guarantees is not a story of the bundle, and a story with a commit has at least one obligation (story_runner.py:152-153). A suffix test would pin a label.

entries.grounds: `{k: v for k, v in row.items() if k != 'story'}` becomes `k != ''`: no key is ever '', so each entry keeps its `story`, the key of the group it sits under (row['story'] = o.story_id at :300 and out.setdefault(row['story'], ...) at :385 are the same value by construction). I re-ran the implementer's differential (diff.py explain) on calc-3-stories, sealed and fully approved: the outputs differ only by an added `story` key in each of the 5 entries, mutant entry == {**original entry, 'story': group} for all 10 (sealed + approved); every other field, entry order, story order and `project` are identical. entries.grounds: Differs: `BC-X does not compile: ...` instead of `contract BC-X does not compile: ...`. The reader is the operator (`refused: ...` on stderr, exit 2). What it needs stays: the refused object's id (L106 {c.id}), the stage ('does not compile'; this loop compiles only contracts, never requirement, criterion or story ids) and the compiler's cause. Measured by me on the mutant: UnapprovedContract (approvals []) -> 'BC-... does not compile: contract BC-... is not approved: ...' (the cause repeats the label); CompileError (HTTP_ROUTE contract, no probe in this release) -> 'BC-V22-S-3.1-a does not compile: no probe declared for subject kind http_route', where the wrapper alone carries the id and 'does not compile' + 'subject kind' still mark it as a contract. Contract ids are any non-empty string (contract.py BehaviorContract.__post_init__), so the label is not redundant by validation, but the id plus the stage phrase is unambiguous. No code, test or document parses or compares the text. A test could only pin the noun before an identifier the mutant keeps: wording, not a contract. Consistent with T03b's final test for [81], which asserts the id, 'does not compile' and the cause and was reviewed to leave 'contract ' unpinned.

entries.group: T06-JUDGE-HOME-SENTINEL: a guard that differs only when a real, non-empty host directory named /nonexistent is mounted.
entries.grounds: Original guard `home != '/nonexistent'`, mutant `home != ''` (L409). `home` is never '' (_probe L291 `env.get('HOME') or '/nonexistent'`), so the mutant always applies the listing check, the original skips it exactly when home is the string '/nonexistent' (the placeholder for an absent or empty HOME, or a literal HOME=/nonexistent, same string). For every other home both guards are True and the programs agree. For home == '/nonexistent' the guards DISAGREE (False/True); the outcomes still agree unless `ls -A /nonexistent` inside lists an entry no mount below it names (names L406-407 excludes at == home): the probe lists $5 only `if [ -e "$5" ]` (PROBE L60), and /nonexistent exists inside only as (a) the parent bubblewrap makes for a mount below it, where every listed entry is that mount's own name (shown <= names holds in both), or (b) itself a bind of a HOST directory /nonexistent with content. (b) needs that directory on the host AND bound by the wrapper: an operator read_only entry (wrap L160-162 refuses a missing one), the client's directory (exe directly in /nonexistent), the workspace, a bare common git directory at /nonexistent; the configuration directory ends in 'opencode' and every other mount is a fixed path (SYSTEM links/dirs, /proc, /dev, /tmp, the HOME tmpfs). Nothing the wrapper builds creates /nonexistent, and by convention it names a path that does not exist. In that state the original admits and the mutant refuses with a 'HOME shows more...' problem although no HOME is set: a false refusal, fail-closed; no breach is admitted by either. Reproduced with the implementer's differential grid on my checkout: the only differing inputs are listings at the placeholder that no mount below it names.

entries.group: T09-EQ-NOFOLLOW: O_NOFOLLOW beside O_CREAT|O_EXCL; O_EXCL already refuses a final-component symbolic link
entries.grounds: Equivalence holds. Proof: O_NOFOLLOW only governs the final path component and O_CREAT|O_EXCL already refuses a final component that exists, a symbolic link included, with EEXIST regardless of its target: POSIX open(), the macOS open(2) man page on this host (`If O_EXCL is set with O_CREAT and the last component of the pathname is a symbolic link, open() will fail even if the symbolic link points to a non-existent name`), Linux open(2), and (recalled, not readable here) Linux build_open_flags ORing O_NOFOLLOW in for O_CREAT|O_EXCL. Where os has no O_NOFOLLOW (Windows) getattr(os,'O_NOFOLLOW',0) is already 0, the mutant's value. The only handler is `except FileExistsError` at L148, and EEXIST is what every state gives. Separate observation, not this mutant (see issues): a dangling link as the NEWEST generation raises a raw FileNotFoundError at L126 (path.read_bytes()), not through os.open.

entries.group: T28-EQ-ROLE-AT-CANDIDATE: the label reaches route() only and every CANDIDATE row is role-independent (own trace per mutant, own label)
entries.grounds: Re-derived from BASE c4c1720, not taken from the hand-over. Value flow: story_runner.py:247-248 builds `preserved` (`ObligationRole` is read at no other line of that module); :250 `spec_id, role = obligations.get(cid) or preserved[cid]` (the plan's own role wins whenever the cid is one of the story's obligations); :251-253 hands `role` to prove() with the literal point MeasurementPoint.CANDIDATE. In prove() (proof.py:80-111) `role` is read once, at :107 `route(bound, spec, point, role)`; prove() refuses PARENT first (:86-87), and the Proof (:28-37), the probe/evaluated payloads (plain(record), protocol.py:189-200), the proof/verified payload (format3.verified_payload :233-246) and the gate row (`proof:{cid}`) carry no role. In route/row_for (routing.py:96-127) role has three readers: the isinstance guard (:114-115; all three labels are ObligationRole members), the table lookup (:125-126) and the fail-closed text (:102-103). Lookup: every role-keyed row of _EXECUTED is at PARENT (:70, :73, :76); the CANDIDATE rows (:81-85) are keyed role None, so .get((C, sat, reason, label)) misses and the `or` falls to the (C, sat, reason, None) row: the same Route for any label. The text is reachable only when row_for returns None; at CANDIDATE it cannot, by totality: Executed.__post_init__ (outcome.py:43-49) allows a reason only on INDETERMINATE and only an IndeterminateReason, which has exactly PRECONDITION_ABSENT and NON_CONTROLLER_SIGNAL (:28-33); contract_satisfaction (:71-79) yields SATISFIED/UNSATISFIED (reason None) or INDETERMINATE; the table has (C,S,None), (C,U,None), (C,I,PA), (C,I,NCS); UNRUNNABLE/INVALID_SPEC return at routing.py:120-123 before the lookup. Experiment (review/probe_attempt_label_identity.py, corroboration not proof): the real run_story/_attempt/GitWorkspace/two-party proof over three results of the affected PRESERVE criterion at the candidate (UNSATISFIED, SATISFIED, subject ABSENT -> SUBJECT_ABSENT_AT_CANDIDATE), label PRESERVE vs the mutant's label (ObligationRole is substituted in story_runner, which is the mutant exactly): the spy sees the label differ, the whole journal (types and payloads, SHAs/digests normalised by first appearance; BASE-vs-BASE control identical) and the attempt outcomes are identical in all 6 comparisons. Also re-ran the hand-over's routing probe: 56 cells, one Route across the 3 roles. [144] label INTRODUCE: the only place INTRODUCE differs from PRESERVE in the table is the PARENT PRECONDITION_ABSENT row (routing.py:70 READY vs :73 PRECONDITION_BROKEN); PARENT is refused by prove() before any role is read, so that row is unreachable from this call site. INTRODUCE is not a foreign label here either: the same loop proves the story's own INTRODUCE obligations at the candidate through the identical prove() call (obligations_of, proof.py:114-116).

entries.grounds: HARNESS L29 False->True is `said.acquire(blocking=False)` -> `blocking=True` in conclude(), reached only from the daemon Timer built in deadline() (cli_invocation.py:718-720; timer is never joined or cancelled). `said` (703) is acquired at 711 (settle, non-blocking) and 714 (conclude) and never released anywhere in the script, so after the first successful acquire it stays held for the life of the process. A blocking acquire on a free lock returns at once and writes RESULT/END exactly like the non-blocking one; on a held lock the non-blocking call returns without writing and the blocking call never returns and therefore never writes: protocol file, RESULT winner, exit status identical. entries.grounds: `spec.origin and spec.has_location` vs `or` differ only on (bool(origin), has_location) = (T,F) or (F,T). Every spec given to inside() (single call at 807) comes from PathFinder.find_spec (resolve at 802/804, the __main__ lookup at 806); under -I -S sys.path_hooks is exactly zipimporter + FileFinder (printed by my spec_pairs.py). A PathFinder spec is either spec_from_file_location (origin=location and _set_fileattr=True set together -> (T,T); also for zipimporter, which goes spec_from_loader -> spec_from_file_location because it has get_filename) or a namespace portion ModuleSpec(name, None) whose origin PathFinder.find_spec sets to None (CPython >= 3.7; requires-python >= 3.11) -> (F,F). (T,F) is only produced by spec_from_loader for loaders without get_filename (built-in/frozen importers), which PathFinder never consults; (F,T) cannot be built. Corroboration (not the proof): spec_pairs.py on 3.14.7 under -I -S over 291 specs (stdlib roots incl. __pycache__ dirs, a tree with regular, namespace, empty dir, module, sourceless .pyc, and a zip with module, package and namespace): 287 (T,T), 4 (F,F), 0 mixed.
